evidence.evidence_paraphrase: SERS is described as using gold, silver, or platinum nanostructures; localized enhanced fields produce stronger Raman signals, while nanoparticle variability can cause nonreproducible results.
A separate SERS example attributes strong signals to plasmon coupling between aggregated functionalized gold nanoparticles, without comparing dispersed and dried states of the same preparation.

assessments.scientific_rationale: The review discusses SERS using metallic nanostructures, including silver and gold, and notes strong enhancement and nanoparticle-related reproducibility problems. However, it does not establish a paired solution-to-dried comparison of the same Ag-shell core-satellite preparation, nor a drying-induced normalized intensity or peak-profile transformation.

evidence.evidence_paraphrase: SERS is explained through surface-plasmon interaction with metallic nanostructures and localized electromagnetic-field enhancement near the nanostructure surface.
SERRS is described as combining SERS enhancement near plasmon-supporting nanostructures with resonance enhancement, but no architecture-specific gap-sweep relation is given.

assessments.scientific_rationale: The review provides general SERS mechanism: metallic nanostructures support surface plasmons and create localized enhanced electromagnetic fields near the metal surface. This supports the broad hotspot-coupling mechanism, but the supplied text does not establish a controlled directional response to polymer-defined inner/outer gap variation in an Ag-bridge architecture.
